title: Create an identity pool and the role it hands out
kills: "A Cognito user pool hands AWS credentials to the app."
cost: $0. Identity pools are provided at no charge, and IAM roles have no additional charge.
cost_if_forgotten: $0 a day. Delete both resources anyway, so that no unused role and no unused identity pool stay in the account.
read_only_alternative: Use this when your account allows no new resources. It changes nothing. List the identity pools with aws cognito-identity list-identity-pools --max-results 10. Pick one identity pool ID as <IDENTITY_POOL_ID> and read its roles with aws cognito-identity get-identity-pool-roles --identity-pool-id <IDENTITY_POOL_ID>. Then read the example trust policy on the Amazon Cognito page "IAM roles": find the aud condition that names the identity pool.

steps.text: Open AWS CloudShell. Create an identity pool that allows no guests. It has no sign-in provider yet: a real app connects its user pool here.
steps.expect: No output. IDENTITY_POOL_ID now holds the identity pool ID: your Region, a colon and a long code.

steps.text: Read the identity pool. Look for users or user profiles in the output.
steps.expect: The pool ID, the name, AllowUnauthenticatedIdentities false and the two tags. No users and no profiles: the identity pool keeps no user profiles.

steps.text: Create the IAM role for signed-in users of this identity pool. Its trust policy names the identity pool (aud) and signed-in users (amr), not a user pool. The role gets no permissions policy.
steps.command: aws iam create-role --role-name saa-identity-federation-t02-auth --assume-role-policy-document "{\"Version\":\"2012-10-17\",\"Statement\":[{\"Effect\":\"Allow\",\"Principal\":{\"Federated\":\"cognito-identity.amazonaws.com\"},\"Action\":\"sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity\",\"Condition\":{\"StringEquals\":{\"cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:aud\":\"$IDENTITY_POOL_ID\"},\"ForAnyValue:StringLike\":{\"cognito-identity.amazonaws.com:amr\":\"authenticated\"}}}]}" --tags Key=book,Value=saa Key=task,Value=identity-federation-t02
steps.expect: No output. ROLE_ARN now holds the ARN of saa-identity-federation-t02-auth.

steps.text: Break it on purpose: replace the trust policy with one that keeps the amr check and drops the aud condition.
steps.expect: An error from IAM. The role keeps the trust policy from step 3.
steps.predict: The new policy still checks that the user signed in. Will IAM save it without the aud condition?
steps.explain: With cognito-identity.amazonaws.com as the principal, IAM does not let a trust policy [permit any identity pool to assume the role](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-identity-pool-trust-policy-aud-condition-enforced). The policy needs an aud condition that names your identity pool: without it, [IAM returns an error](../facts/cognito.md#cognito-identity-pool-trust-policy-aud-condition-enforced). The amr check alone is not enough.

steps.text: No fix is needed: the safe trust policy from step 3 is still in place. Attach the role to the identity pool as its authenticated role.
Read the roles of the identity pool. This mapping is where a sign-in turns into temporary AWS credentials.
steps.expect: authenticated, with the ARN of saa-identity-federation-t02-auth. There is no unauthenticated role, because the pool allows no guests. The role belongs to the identity pool, not to a user pool.

verify.expect: An empty list: the identity pool is gone. The tagging API does not list IAM roles, so also run aws iam get-role --role-name saa-identity-federation-t02-auth and expect a NoSuchEntity error: the role is gone too.

still_costs: Nothing after the cleanup. Identity pools are provided at no charge, and IAM has no additional charge.

The verify list does not show IAM roles: GetResources does not currently support IAM users and roles. Check the role with aws iam get-role --role-name saa-identity-federation-t02-auth and expect an error that the role does not exist.
If the CloudShell session ended before the cleanup, IDENTITY_POOL_ID is empty. Find the pool ID again with aws cognito-identity list-identity-pools --max-results 10.
